acceptance: Every base image contains no model-written text, letters, numbers or visible faces.
Every rendered text element comes from the programmatic overlay layer and the audited fact source.
Images placed in the deliverable are neither stretched nor cropped away, confirmed by real rendering.
Asset integrity gate passes and its negative control has been executed.

failure_modes.failure: Generated base image contains model-written text or gibberish
failure_modes.response: Remove the writable carrier from the subject description, regenerate, and re-run the screening gate.

failure_modes.failure: Overlay labels do not match what the scene actually shows
failure_modes.response: Correct the override table against the audited specification; do not invent a second set of wording.

failure_modes.failure: Batch generation silently returns zero images
failure_modes.response: Reduce the batch to five requests or fewer and resume; never treat an empty batch as success.

capabilities.limits: Method and scripts only. It does not certify generation quality by itself: every base image still needs human inspection, and a style prompt is not a brand guideline.

outputs.purpose: vis-concept-illustration result linked to task and acceptance evidence

scenarios: Produce the vis-concept-illustration deliverable in a scoped reporting or presentation task.
Raise a report or deck whose illustrations are line diagrams and cannot show a real scene, texture or build.
workflow: Read only the task, the declared authoritative content source and the existing figure specification.
Write one subject description per figure: state counts, positions and blank carriers; keep every carrier unmarked.
Generate the text-free base images, then run the text-screening gate and inspect every base image before compositing.
Draw all titles, component names, criteria and disclaimers with the programmatic overlay layer from the audited fact source.
Compress to JPEG q94 with 4:4:4 chroma, verify the pixel difference against the reference, and place images without distortion.
Verify the deliverable, record the actual gate result, and link current claims before handoff.

acceptance: Every design rule in scope has a picture, at least two testable constraints, a mechanism and a failure mode.
The failure mode is named inside the mechanism paragraph and is a verbatim substring of the fact source.
Every figure follows one of the three body routes; the only unacceptable form is a skeleton drawing that outlines a part and adds text labels where a filled body would have carried the relation.
Every number printed on a figure is traceable to the fact source; numbers without a source stay in the constraint list only.
Every body declares its verdict explicitly; an undeclared verdict fails the gate and is never read as neutral.
The English version contains no Chinese characters including the footer declaration, and all eight gates were executed with a negative control.

failure_modes.failure: Rule delivered as a skeleton drawing: a part outlined with text labels and no filled body
failure_modes.response: Redraw it as a filled engineering section or isometric solid. Keep a symbolic relation diagram only when the rule is about two reference quantities and the picture has no part in it.

failure_modes.failure: A valid filled engineering section is rejected because it has no three lit faces
failure_modes.response: That rejection is wrong: a filled section with hatching, leader lines and dimensions is an accepted body form. Judge the picture by the skeleton rule, not by a single lighting recipe.

failure_modes.failure: The mechanism paragraph restates the rule instead of explaining it
failure_modes.response: State why the rule exists - shrinkage rate, cooling order, fibre orientation, stress concentration - and rewrite the paragraph.

failure_modes.failure: The failure mode appears only in the constraint list, so the reader never learns what breaks
failure_modes.response: Name the failure inside the mechanism paragraph and keep the wording a verbatim excerpt of the fact source.

failure_modes.failure: A body's verdict is left undeclared and is silently read as neutral
failure_modes.response: Declare good, bad or neutral explicitly. An absent verdict fails the gate; it must not be filled in by a default.

failure_modes.failure: A good and a bad body are ordered so the bad one sits on the left
failure_modes.response: Order good-left and bad-right at load time. Exception: a parameter sequence such as too small, right, too large keeps its semantic order.

failure_modes.failure: A number printed on the figure cannot be traced to the fact source
failure_modes.response: Remove it from the figure, keep it in the constraint list, and fix the source table.

capabilities.limits: Method and scripts only. It does not certify that a drawn body is physically accurate: every figure still needs human inspection, and a rule set is engineering judgement, not vendor data. The gate judges structure, traceability and bilingual purity - it cannot judge whether a drawing is a good drawing.

outputs.purpose: vis-dfm-illustration result linked to task and acceptance evidence

scenarios: Produce the vis-dfm-illustration deliverable in a design-rule or process-criterion chapter.

workflow: List every design rule in scope from the audited fact source; one rule is one panel.
For each rule write the testable constraints, the mechanism and the failure mode; a rule without a mechanism is not done.
State the failure mode in the mechanism paragraph as well, and keep it a verbatim excerpt of the fact source.
Choose one of the three body routes: A text-free generated scene, B a filled engineering section or isometric solid, or C a symbolic relation diagram with no part in it.
Assemble the panel with the programmatic layer so every number and every label comes from the fact source.
Run the eight gates - coverage, bilingual purity including the footer, numeric self-consistency, verbatim failure mode, anchor on ink, verdict completeness, layout, negative control.
Verify the deliverable, record the actual gate result, and link current claims before handoff.

acceptance: Baseline and comparison identify client, profile, model, task mix, time window, source and configuration.

acceptance: Each reported client state is backed by the client's own tool list or a live launch result, not by a governance file.

failure_modes.failure: No client-side evidence for the capability state
failure_modes.response: Mark the state unknown or unattested and obtain a live launch attempt before claiming either support or a limitation.

failure_modes.failure: A token or concurrency measure requires removing background execution
failure_modes.response: Reject the measure; background concurrency is never the token lever.

failure_modes.failure: The client product, not governance, blocks background execution
failure_modes.response: Record a client-side limitation with the host policy evidence and use a supported path; never patch the client bundle.

capabilities.limits: Provides measurement and governance guidance. It cannot grant a client a capability its product withholds, and it never claims runtime behavior without the client's own evidence. outputs.purpose: Per-client background execution state with the client's own rejection evidence or live handle.

workflow: Read protocols/BACKGROUND-AGENT-EXECUTION.md and the current client adapter record.

Never implement a token reduction by disabling background execution; escalate a client-side product limit as a client-side limit.

acceptance: Scan and learning coverage are complete within the declared roots, or the exclusion is explicit.

failure_modes.response: Keep AgentOS routing authoritative and record the overlap as reference-only.

Strengthen an existing capability when the learning fits it; register a new capability when it is a real gap.
Produce the reviewed, gated and published corpus update, then read the remote state back.
